does: Washes food in cold water, to carry off grit, loose starch, or the salt and brine it was kept in.

intro.what: Rinsing uses cold water to remove loose grit, starch or excess brine.
intro.why: It teaches you to remove unwanted residue while keeping the flavour and texture you want.

how: Put the food in a colander, or in a large bowl of cold water.
Run cold water over it, or move it about in the bowl with your hands.
Change the water until it stays clear. Lift leaves out of the water, so that the grit stays behind.
Drain it well, and dry whatever will be fried or dressed.

cues.text: The last water stays as clear as it went in.
Brined food tastes pleasantly salty and no longer harsh.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring washed leaves and their water out together, so that the grit lands back on them.
mistakes.fix: Lift the leaves out and leave the grit at the bottom.

mistakes.mistake: Rinsing sauerkraut or capers until none of their sharpness is left.
mistakes.fix: Taste as you go, and stop while they still have bite.

quiz.question: What can rinsing remove from food?
choices: Only dirt visible on the outside.
Loose grit, starch or excess brine.
All salt and flavour throughout the food.
quiz.because: Cold water carries away loose material or excess brine, depending on the food.

quiz.question: How should washed leaves leave a bowl of water?
choices: Tip leaves and water through a sieve together.
Stir the grit back up before draining.
Lift them out before emptying the bowl.
quiz.because: Lifting separates the leaves from grit that has settled beneath them.

quiz.question: What tasting cue guides rinsing brined food?
choices: It remains pleasantly salty without harsh brine.
It loses every trace of sharpness.
It tastes exactly as harsh as before.
quiz.because: Rinsing should moderate excess brine without washing away the food’s intended character.

quiz.question: Rinsed capers lost their sharpness. What would you change next time?
choices: Rinse longer to equalise their flavour.
Taste as you rinse and stop while they retain bite.
Soak them in fresh water until bland.
quiz.because: Checking flavour prevents excessive rinsing from removing the sharpness that makes the ingredient useful.
